name: Chōchin-obake
description: Chōchin-obake is a Japanese yōkai depicted as an old paper lantern (chōchin) that has split open along its bamboo ribs to reveal a single eye, a long protruding tongue, and a wide mouth — a classic example of a tsukumogami, an everyday object brought to life after long use.

aliases.name: Bura-bura
aliases.meaning: literally 'dangle-dangle'; name used by Toriyama Sekien for a hanging lantern yōkai

regions: Edo (modern Tokyo) — primary publishing centre for the imagery
Kyoto and Osaka — kabuki and ukiyo-e production
Nationwide via mass-produced karuta, kusazōshi, and toy prints
origin: The chōchin-obake is a creature of the Japanese popular imagination, attested across the Japanese archipelago through printed illustration and stage drama, with no specific regional folk-legend tradition.
